theater: 幼發拉底河中游與哈布爾河谷

battle.name: 漢摩拉比對亞述的戰爭
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河中游與哈布爾河谷
battle.brief: 前1760年前後，巴比倫王漢摩拉比聯同埃什努納、埃蘭轉兵北上，與亞述王沙姆希阿達德一世及後繼者在美索不達米亞中游交戰，攻破亞述都城舒巴特恩利爾，亞述政權就此崩解。卡面的埃及長矛屬前3200年早王朝工藝，比本役早一千四百多年，並不在此戰場上；當時定勝負的是銅矛、複合弓與輕型戰車。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方，是剛從兩河南部打到北部的巴比倫王國，與控制美索不達米亞北部一整片城邦的亞述王國；背景還有三方聯盟與亞述介入幼發拉底河中游的角力。巴比倫一方是古巴比倫王朝的王國，核心在巴比倫城與尼普爾，疆域自南部的烏魯克、拉爾薩一路伸到幼發拉底河中游的馬里、希帕拉與提爾西普；它沒有常備軍，出征靠王令臨時徵召的民軍與王室侍從，兵種為持矛步兵、弓手與輕型戰車隊，攻城所需工兵與糧秣由神廟的田租與配給制度供應。亞述一方此時還是古亞述時期的政權，國都在哈布爾河谷的舒巴特恩利爾，王為阿摩魯特人沙姆希阿達德一世，另有幼發拉底河畔的埃卡拉圖姆為第二都城；他以吞併哈布爾河上游諸邦起家，控制哈布爾河、幼發拉底河中游與巴利赫河谷，商隊與總督駐在這些從屬城邑收取貢賦，並把手伸向埃布拉與阿拉拉赫方向的商路。真正改變局勢的是第三方：埃什努納王辛-伊德南、埃蘭王，以及北方阿勒頗的亞姆哈德王國先後轉而與巴比倫站在同一陣線，《同步史》稱此為三方國王的聯合攻勢。
countriesEn: The belligerents in this war were Babylonia, a southern kingdom that had just driven its armies up the Euphrates to the middle of the river, and Assyria, a northern state that had absorbed the city-states of the upper Khabur and now controlled the corridor between the two great rivers. Babylonia was a kingdom of the Old Babylonian dynasty: its core lay at Babylon and Nippur, and its territory ran from Uruk and Larsa in the south up through Mari, Sippar and Til Barsip on the middle Euphrates. It had no standing army; campaigns were raised on royal orders from a conscripted citizen levy, with spear-armed infantry, archers and light chariot detachments, while the temples' estates and ration system supplied the food and the siege equipment. Assyria at this moment was still an early Assyrian polity: its capital was Shubat-Enlil in the Khabur valley and its king was Shamshi-Adad I, an Amorite who had taken the throne; a second capital, Ekallatum, stood on the Euphrates. He had risen by absorbing the cities of the upper Khabur, and from that base Assyria held the Khabur, the middle Euphrates and the Balib valley, with royal officials and tax collectors posted in the dependent towns and its reach extended towards the caravan roads of Ebla and Aleppo. What truly changed the situation, however, were the third parties: Sin-iddinam of Eshnunna, the king of Elam, and the rulers of Yamhad in the north all ended up on the same side as Babylon, and the Synchronistic History describes the three kings joining in a common offensive.
people: 主角是巴比倫王漢摩拉比，阿摩魯特王朝君主辛-穆巴利特之子，約前1792年即位，統治四十三年，前1750年病逝。他在本役之前已滅埃什努納、掃平拉爾薩、擊退埃蘭，再沿幼發拉底河打到馬里，把戰線推入亞述腹地；他留下的兩百五十餘封書信，至今仍是重建本役前後兩河政局最密的材料。亞述一方的核心是沙姆希阿達德一世，阿摩魯特人出身，約前1809年奪取舒巴特恩利爾而成亞述之王，經營哈布爾與巴利赫河谷，並把女兒嫁與駐守埃卡拉圖姆的兒子雅斯瑪海德一世；《同步史》記載他在戰敗後西走，投奔亞姆哈德與埃布拉，最終死於敗亡之地；其子雅斯瑪海德一世約前1776至前1760年在位，未能扭轉崩局。第三位關鍵人物是阿達德-尼拉里三世，約前1760年繼位，是中亞述時期的奠基者，他重建亞述、填補阿蘭與赫梯留下的空隙，把國家從城邦聯盟改造成帝國。北方方面，亞姆哈德王國的亞里姆-里姆一世在戰事中陣亡，其子阿卜迪-米爾庫蒂接位後仍捲入與赫梯的衝突，最後也戰死。同一時期在幼發拉底河上游與亞述交兵的赫梯王哈圖西里三世，是這場北線危機的另一方推手。巴比倫一方的具體戰場指揮者姓名多不見於同期材料，只有書吏、祭司與神廟財官在文獻中留下痕跡。
peopleEn: The central figure is Hammurabi, king of Babylon, son of the Amorite ruler Sin-Muballit, who took the throne around 1792 BC and reigned for forty-three years, dying of illness at Babylon in 1750 BC. Before this war he had already destroyed Eshnunna, crushed Larsa, turned back Elam, marched up the Euphrates to Mari and pushed the front into the Assyrian heartland; more than 250 of his own letters survive and remain the densest source for the politics of the two rivers around this campaign. On the Assyrian side stands Shamshi-Adad I, an Amorite by origin who seized Shubat-Enlil around 1809 BC and became king of Assyria, holding the Khabur and Balib valleys and installing his son Yasmah-Adad I at Ekallatum on the Euphrates; the Synchronistic History says that after his defeat he fled west to Yamhad and Ebla and died there in ruin, and his son Yasmah-Adad I, who reigned roughly from 1776 to 1760 BC, could not reverse the collapse. The third key figure is Adad-nirari III, who came to the throne around 1760 BC and founded the Middle Assyrian period, rebuilding Assyria, filling the gaps left by Aram and Hittite rivals, and turning a loose union of city-states into an empire. In the north, Yarim-Lim I of Yamhad was killed during the fighting; his son Abdi-Milkuti succeeded him, remained entangled in the conflict with the Hatti, and also died in battle. The Hittite king Hattusili III, who fought Assyria on the upper Euphrates in the same years, was the other driving force behind this crisis in the north. Hammurabi's own subordinates are rarely named in contemporary sources: only scribes, priests and temple treasurers leave a trace in the documents.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬早王朝時期、主前3200年左右的工藝：銅或青銅矛頭以繩索或瀝青綁在木桿上，埃及人用它守城垣，也用它收復失地。就年代而言，它比本役早一千四百餘年，並不出現在這個戰場；就形制而言，它與本役美索不達米亞步兵手中的長矛同屬「銅矛頭綁木桿」的工藝譜系，是可以拿來對照的先例，而不是作戰裝備。本役真正在場的兵器如下：步兵的銅矛、銅斧與短劍，弓手所用的複合反曲弓與銅鏃，車兵裝備的輕型戰車——在這個時期多以驢或野驢挽曳，馬匹仍屬奢侈品，車上乘員為射手加槍手；防護方面有皮甲，以軟皮或皮條層層綴合，亞述與巴比倫的精銳多著此甲上陣，銅盔則只配給車兵與軍官級骨幹。攻城方面備有撞槌、掘道用的土工器具與填壕的柴石，鐵器極少見，斧鋌仍以銅為主。運輸與補給靠幼發拉底河水路、驢車與人力扛運，軍中另備驛馬與信鴿傳令，並攜帶繩索與量器作行軍丈量。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card belongs to the Early Dynastic period, around 3200 BC: a copper or bronze head lashed with cord or bitumen to a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold walls and to reconquer lost ground. Chronologically it predates this campaign by more than fourteen centuries and played no part in it; typologically, however, it belongs to the same family of copper head bound to a wooden shaft that the Mesopotamian infantry of this war carried, so it is a usable parallel rather than a piece of equipment that was on the field. The weapons actually present were these: infantry spears, axes and short swords of copper; the composite recurve bow with copper arrowheads used by the archers; and the light war chariot, at this date normally drawn by donkeys or onagers, with horses still a rarity, carrying a driver, a shooter and a spear-armed guard. Protection was leather armour, layers of hide or leather strips lashed together, worn by the elite of both Assyria and Babylon, while copper helmets went to the charioteers and to the officer class. Siege work brought battering rams, earth-moving tools for tunnelling, and brushwood and stone for filling ditches; iron was scarce and the axes and adzes of the age were still largely of copper. Supply and transport rode the Euphrates, with boats, donkey trains and porters, while relay horses and carrier pigeons carried despatches and the army carried cords and measures for reckoning distance on the march.
tactics: 巴比倫的打法在漢摩拉比手中已經定型，是一套以攻城與殘破遠征為主的作戰方式。開春集結兵員，順幼發拉底河北上，遠征隊在河谷中分為水陸兩路：船隊運載糧秣與攻城器材，車隊與步兵沿東岸道路前進，遇城即圍。攻城時先以土壘與壕溝封閉城外通道，再築土坡貼近城牆，以撞槌連續撞擊牆基，同時派工兵掘地道、填壕、封堵城門破口；城破之後並不設官治理，而是拆毀城牆、擄走神像、遣散人口——本役對舒巴特恩利爾與馬里的處理，即是此一作風的兩次示範。兵種配合上，車隊用於野戰與追擊，弓手列於兩翼，步兵持矛結陣居中，車兵掩護步兵接近城牆。巴比倫更高明的一步是三面用兵：自己北上攻亞述，同時拉攏埃什努納與埃蘭，使亞述無法在南方抽兵，只能死守北線。亞述的反制則依靠其車隊與弓手在幼發拉底河與哈布爾河之間的縱深據點，並以王命調度從屬城邑的守軍與援兵；一旦都城與交通線同時失去，陣地便節節後退，《同步史》記載其敗後向西逃入亞姆哈德與埃布拉境內求助。
tacticsEn: Babylon's way of fighting had already been fixed under Hammurabi, and it centred on siege and destructive expedition. Troops mustered in spring and moved north along the Euphrates, the expedition splitting into a water column and a land column: boats carrying food and siege material, carts and infantry following the eastern track, and every city on the way being invested at once. The besiegers first closed the approaches with embankments and ditches, then built earthen ramps against the walls, drove the rams against the wall foot, and sent sappers to dig under the foundations, to fill the ditches and to seal the breaches at the gates; and when the city fell it was not administered but dismantled, the walls pulled down, the gods carried off and the population dispersed. The destruction of Shubat-Enlil and of Mari are the two demonstrations of that method. In the field, chariots were used for shock and pursuit, archers were deployed on the wings, and spearmen held the centre in a close formation, the charioteers screening the infantry as they closed on the walls. Babylon's sharper move was to fight on three fronts: pressing north against Assyria while holding Eshnunna and Elam in the south, so that Assyria could not detach troops from its northern front and could only hold in depth. Assyria's counter relied on chariots and archers distributed among strongholds between the Euphrates and the Khabur, and on royal orders summoning the garrisons and reliefs of the dependent towns; once capital and road were lost together, the position fell back step by step, and the Synchronistic History records the king fleeing west into Yamhad and Ebla in search of help.
data: 可核的數字大致如下，並須先說明年代體系的分歧：漢摩拉比在位四十三年，通行中年代把其統治定於約前1792至前1750年，修訂版則為前1784至前1742年，各家年代體系最遠可差近兩百年，因此本役只能給出概數，戰爭落在其統治的最後數年、約當在位第三十至三十三年，與此役相關的巴比倫年名，多為「他擊敗了蘇巴爾圖的軍隊」一類的表述。亞述王的在位年表約為：沙姆希阿達德一世約前1809至前1776年，雅斯瑪海德一世約前1776至前1760年，阿達德-尼拉里三世約前1760至前1745年。城市方面，馬里被毀於約前1761年（有定前1762年者），舒巴特恩利爾在約前1760年前後遭毀而廢棄，亞述重心此後北移。馬里書信保存了前1774至前1761年間的兩河政治往來，泥板逾兩萬片，其中漢摩拉比本人的信件就有兩百五十封以上，本役的經過正是靠這批文書才得以重建。距離上，巴比倫至馬里順幼發拉底河行程約五百公里，馬里至舒巴特恩利爾沿陸路約三百五十公里。兵員、陣亡數與攻城耗時在同期文獻中完全沒有留下可靠記載，本節不列臆測數字；戰爭的月份亦無依據，編年只給年份，此處按兩河春末的行軍季節取四月。
dataEn: The verifiable figures run as follows, after one warning about chronologies. Hammurabi reigned forty-three years; the middle chronology dates his rule to about 1792-1750 BC while the revised chronology gives 1784-1742 BC, and the various systems differ by nearly two centuries, so this campaign can only be placed approximately, in the last years of his reign, roughly his thirtieth to thirty-third regnal year; the Babylonian year-names attached to those years are of the type 'he defeated the army of Subartu'. The Assyrian sequence of reigns runs: Shamshi-Adad I, about 1809-1776 BC; Yasmah-Adad I, about 1776-1760 BC; Adad-nirari III, about 1760-1745 BC. On the towns: Mari was destroyed about 1761 BC, some chronologies giving 1762, and Shubat-Enlil was wrecked and abandoned around 1760 BC, after which the centre of Assyria shifted north. The Mari letters preserve the diplomatic traffic of the two rivers between about 1774 and 1761 BC; the archive holds more than twenty thousand tablets, among them over 250 written by Hammurabi himself, and it is on this material that the course of the campaign has been reconstructed. As for distances, the river route from Babylon to Mari is about 500 km and the land route from Mari to Shubat-Enlil some 350 km. Troop strengths, casualties and the length of each siege leave no reliable trace in contemporary texts, so no figures are offered for them; the month of the war is likewise unrecorded, the annals give only the year, and April is used here on the grounds of the late-spring campaigning season of the two rivers.
cause: 打起來是多層積累的結果。第一層是地緣：亞述在沙姆希阿達德一世手中統一哈布爾河上游諸邦，控制了從幼發拉底河中游通往安納托利亞的商路，並把勢力伸進巴比倫的北翼，兩國的邊界在幼發拉底河中游正面相接，中間沒有緩衝地帶。第二層是聯盟：巴比倫、埃什努納與埃蘭三方的君主一度結盟對付亞述，《同步史》記載三方合兵，亞述一度處於被圍攻的地位；亞述也曾支持埃什努納的叛離，使巴比倫腹背受敵。第三層是資源：北方出木材、銅料與馬匹，南方出穀物、椰棗與織物，幼發拉底河中游是唯一把兩者接在一起的走廊，誰控制這條走廊，誰就控制兩河的貿易稅。第四層是體質：巴比倫是集中王權加神廟官僚的國家，能連年動員、遠征與築城；亞述此時仍是由征服而來的王國加眾多從屬城邦的鬆散集合，一旦都城與交通線同時失去，國家便迅速解體。第五層是直接導火線：亞述介入巴比倫與埃什努納、拉爾薩之間的戰事，使漢摩拉比無法容忍北方強國站在自己的側翼，於是先滅埃什努納、再取馬里，最後才把矛頭指向亞述。同期還有第三股力量在旁觀並趁勢而動——赫梯王哈圖西里三世正沿幼發拉底河上溯與亞述交兵，任何一方都清楚這條河谷的爭奪已牽動整個近東。
causeEn: War came from several layers of cause. The first is geography: Assyria, unified by Shamshi-Adad I over the cities of the upper Khabur, held the trade road running from the middle Euphrates towards Anatolia and pushed its reach into Babylonia's northern flank, so that the two states faced each other across the middle Euphrates with no buffer between them. The second is alliance: the kings of Babylon, Eshnunna and Elam at one point combined against Assyria, the Synchronistic History describing the three joining their armies and the Assyrian kingship briefly besieged; Assyria in turn had supported Eshnunna's defection, keeping the rear of Babylonia under pressure. The third is resources: the north yields timber, copper and horses, the south grain, dates and cloth, and the middle Euphrates is the one corridor that joins the two, so whoever holds that corridor collects the trade dues of the whole land. The fourth is the character of the two states: Babylonia, a concentrated kingship supported by a temple bureaucracy, could mobilise, campaign and build for year on year; Assyria was still a kingdom of conquest loosely holding a bundle of dependent towns, and once capital and road were lost together, the state came apart quickly. The fifth is the immediate spark: Assyrian intervention in the wars between Babylon, Eshnunna and Larsa made it impossible for Hammurabi to tolerate a great power on his flank, so he answered by destroying Eshnunna, then taking Mari, and only then turned his spear against Assyria. A third force was moving in the same valley throughout: the Hittite king Hattusili III was working his way up the Euphrates and fighting Assyria, and every ruler in the region knew that the struggle for that river had come to concern the whole Near East.
impact: 本役的後果超出戰場本身。第一，亞述王國的舊秩序被打碎：舒巴特恩利爾被毀而廢棄，哈布爾河上游諸邦的城邑網絡中斷，阿達德-尼拉里三世重建國土時，只能改以小亞細亞與上美索不達米亞的重新征服為基礎，中亞述時期的帝國模型由此成形，而不再是靠舊有從屬城邦撐起來的聯盟。第二，巴比倫完成了對美索不達米亞的整合：南有拉爾薩、北有亞述、西有埃什努納全數歸入同一王權，幼發拉底河中游的關稅與商路改由巴比倫收取，漢摩拉比在最後十年間的戰爭帶來兩河數百年來第一次真正的政治統一。第三，經濟上是一次重創：馬里作為上幼發拉底河的大港與物流中心被夷平，數千居民被擄往巴比倫，沿河貿易的節點整體南移，直到後來亞述重新控制上游才逐漸恢復。第四，軍事倫理上則立下榜樣：擄走神像、拆毀城牆成為此後數百年近東列強的標準動作，從亞述到赫梯、到後來的亞述帝國，一再重演。第五，它把赫梯拉進了兩河：亞述在河谷的崩解，使哈圖西里三世得以在幼發拉底河上游站穩腳跟，兩河上游的權力平衡從此改由巴比倫與赫梯兩方主導，而亞述此後的復國，正是在這兩面擠壓之下才走另一條路。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached well beyond the battlefield. First, the old order of Assyria was broken: Shubat-Enlil was wrecked and abandoned, the network of towns along the upper Khabur was cut, and Adad-nirari III, rebuilding the country, could found the Middle Assyrian empire only on fresh conquest in Anatolia and upper Mesopotamia rather than on the old network of dependent cities. Second, Babylonia completed the unification of Mesopotamia: Larsa in the south, Assyria in the north and Eshnunna in the west all passed under a single kingship, the dues and roads of the middle Euphrates were collected by Babylon, and the campaigns of Hammurabi's last decade produced the first real political unity the two rivers had known in centuries. Third, the economic cost was severe: Mari, the great harbour and clearing house of the upper Euphrates, was flattened and thousands of its people deported to Babylon, the node of the river trade moving south until Assyria recovered the upper reaches generations later. Fourth, a precedent was set in military ethics: carrying off the gods and pulling down the walls became a standard practice for Near Eastern powers for centuries afterwards, repeated by Assyria, by the Hatti and by the later Assyrian empire. Fifth, the war pulled the Hatti into the rivers: with Assyria collapsing in the valley, Hattusili III gained a foothold on the upper Euphrates, and the balance of power in the upper country came to be settled between Babylonia and the Hittites, while the revival of Assyria thereafter would follow a different road under the pressure of both.
result: 結局是巴比倫勝出，而且是壓倒性的勝利。亞述的都城被毀，王室西走，國家在數年之內解體：沙姆希阿達德一世在敗亡中死去，繼位的雅斯瑪海德一世守不住北疆，約前1760年身死，前1760年前後登位的阿達德-尼拉里三世只繼承了一片需要重新收拾的廢墟。巴比倫則趁勢把邊界推到哈布爾河谷，隨後回師南下，在漢摩拉比在位末年徹底解決埃什努納與拉爾薩；前1750年漢摩拉比在巴比倫病逝時，交接的是一個從南部拉爾薩到北部哈布爾河連成一體的國家，他留下的法典石柱正是在這一統一的底色上刻成。需要說明的是：決戰的確切日期、雙方兵員、攻城日程與陣亡數目，在兩河同期文獻中一概沒有留下；能確定的，是這場戰爭把古亞述時期推到終點，把中亞述時期拉開，也把巴比倫推上兩河唯一強國的位置。本役與同期的赫梯—亞述衝突在後世編年中常被混為一談，學界至今對其決戰地點存有異說，本卡只把可確定的部分列為定論。
resultEn: The outcome was a Babylonian victory, and an overwhelming one. The Assyrian capital was destroyed, the royal house fled west, and the state came apart within a few years: Shamshi-Adad I died in his ruin, his successor Yasmah-Adad I could not hold the northern marches and died around 1760 BC, and Adad-nirari III, who took the throne about then, inherited ruins that had to be gathered up again from scratch. Babylon pressed on to the Khabur valley and then turned south, settling Eshnunna and Larsa for good in the closing years of Hammurabi's reign; when he fell ill at Babylon in 1750 BC he bequeathed a state stretching without a break from Larsa in the south to the Khabur in the north, and the law code he carved on the diorite stele was cut against the background of that unity. It should be said plainly that the exact date of the decisive engagement, the strengths on both sides, the duration of the sieges and the casualty figures leave no trace whatever in contemporary Mesopotamian texts; what can be established is that this war closed the early Assyrian period, opened the Middle Assyrian one, and set Babylonia up as the single power of the two rivers. This campaign is often conflated in later chronicles with the contemporary Hittite-Assyrian war, and the exact site of the decisive battle remains disputed; only the firmly established elements are asserted here.
